title: Delayed or Missing CPF Contributions when Platform Workers Switch Platforms
what_it_is: Delayed or Missing CPF Contributions when Platform Workers Switch Platforms

sections.label: Platform worker CPF teething issues
sections.summary: Platform operators had teething issues with inaccurate earnings declarations causing incorrect CPF contributions, which were promptly resolved, and overall collection has been smooth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: There were some teething issues as platform operators adjusted to the new requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This included instances where platform operators declared inaccurate earnings that resulted in platform workers receiving incorrect CPF contributions, due to administrative errors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Where such cases arose, they were promptly resolved and platform workers received their correct CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Overall, the CPF collection for platform workers has been smooth due to the extensive pre-implementation engagements with platform operators and platform associations to iron out operational details.

sections.label: Workers miss CPF on joining
sections.summary: Workers report not receiving CPF contributions for up to two months when joining a new platform operator, and are doubly penalised as most platforms give first-month sign-on incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In the current CPF process, workers have given the feedback that they do not enjoy CPF contributions for up to two months when they first join a new platform operator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: They are also doubly penalised, as most platforms provide special sign-on incentives in the first month of work.

sections.label: Monthly 15th cut-off date
sections.summary: A cut-off date on the 15th of each month balances platform operators' operational ease and sufficient time for accurate contributions, minimising impact on workers' CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: A cut-off date on the 15th of each month is applied, which balances between the operational ease of platform operators and ensuring sufficient time for accurate contributions, while minimising this particular impact to platform workers in building up their CPF savings.

sections.label: Back payment of CPF considered
sections.summary: The Ministry of Manpower has also considered requiring back payment of the CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower has also considered requiring back payment of the CPF contributions.

sections.label: Engaging operators on efficiency
sections.summary: Following feedback, engagement with platform operators has started to assess whether the existing arrangement could be made more efficient while balancing operational requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: Nonetheless, following the feedback, we have started engaging platform operators to assess whether the existing arrangement could be made more efficient while balancing the operational requirements.
